# Kimi K2.7 Swarm Workstation

> Kimi K2.7 Swarm Workstation is a native Windows and Mac desktop app that coordinates up to 300 parallel AI sub-agents, powered by Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.7 Code (1T-parameter MoE, released June 12, 2026). The model scores 81.1% on MCPMark Verified — beating Claude Opus 4.8's 76.4% at tool use — while costing roughly 5× less per token. The app deploys a coordinated "hive" of specialist agents (each with its own MCP toolset, isolated context, and live reasoning stream) to complete in minutes what sequential models take hours to do: deep research, whole-repo coding, legacy migration, competitor analysis, financial data gathering. Features include the Hyper-Parallel Browser, MCP Hive (every agent carries a full MCP toolset), Swarm Bridge (drops into Claude Code / Cursor / OpenClaw as a 5×-cheaper backend), ThoughtStream live reasoning visualization, Local Token Optimizer, Data Fusion Engine (auto PDF/Excel/JSON reports), and Multimodal Swarm Vision. Free Swarm mode via built-in proxy pool, or bring your own Moonshot API key. One-click signed installer.

## Model: Kimi K2.7 Code

- **Developer:** Moonshot AI, released June 12, 2026
- **License:** Modified MIT (open weights on Hugging Face: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.7-Code)
- **Architecture:** 1T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts, ~32B active parameters per token, 384-expert routing, INT4 native quantization
- **Context:** 256K tokens
- **Focus:** Coding and agentic tasks, long-horizon execution, MCP tool use
- **Benchmarks:** MCPMark Verified 81.1% (vs Claude Opus 4.8 76.4%), Kimi Code Bench v2 62.0 (up from K2.6's 50.9, +21.8%), gap to GPT-5.5 narrowed from 18 to 7 points
- **Efficiency:** ~30% fewer thinking-tokens than K2.6
- **Pricing:** ~$0.95 input / $4.00 output per million tokens (vs Opus 4.8 $5/$25)

## Killer Features (desktop build)

- **Hyper-Parallel Browser:** 300 agents crawl simultaneously, each with isolated context, gathering from Amazon/Reddit/LinkedIn/GitHub at once
- **MCP Hive:** every agent carries a full MCP toolset (files, browser, databases, APIs), multiplying K2.7's best-in-class tool use across 300 agents
- **Swarm Bridge:** Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible API lets the swarm drop into Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenClaw as a backend — same power, 5× cheaper than Opus 4.8
- **ThoughtStream:** live visualization of all 300 agents reasoning in real time; click any agent to watch its page, code edits, or reasoning
- **Local Token Optimizer:** prompt-compression layer stacked on K2.7's native ~30% efficiency; Swarm mode runs practically free via proxy pool
- **Data Fusion Engine:** auto-converts collected data into PDF / Excel / JSON reports with proofs and links
- **Multimodal Swarm Vision:** each agent analyzes screenshots and charts on the fly
- **Custom Agent Tuning:** assign roles to agent groups (e.g. 50 find reviews, 50 analyze prices, 200 write code)
- **PARL (Parallel Agent Reinforcement Learning):** proprietary coordination layer eliminating multi-agent coordination errors
- **Critical Steps routing:** auto-detects critical task nodes, floods them with compute, cuts runtime up to 80%

## Use Cases

- Marketing: analyze 100+ competitor ad campaigns at once → full strategy in minutes
- Development: hunt bugs across whole repo via 300 agents → zero critical vulns before deploy
- Legacy migration: 300 agents decompose, test, refactor in parallel → modernized stack + migration plan
- Investing: pull financials of 50 companies at once → comparison table
- Deep Research: scan scientific databases → 50-page summary
- Swarm-as-backend: drive Claude Code / Cursor through the Bridge at 5× lower cost

## Pricing Model

- App: Free
- Swarm mode: Free via built-in proxy pool (most users never pay)
- Optional: bring your own Moonshot API key for unlimited limits
- Underlying model pricing (BYO key): ~$0.95/$4.00 per million tokens

## Platform and Distribution

- **Windows:** 10 and 11, 64-bit, signed .exe installer, RTX 30xx+ recommended for local acceleration
- **macOS:** 12+, Apple Developer ID signed and notarized, native M1/M2/M3/M4/M5
- **Architecture:** Universal macOS binary; Windows x86_64
- **Distribution:** Direct download from GitHub releases, SHA-256 checksums published

## Privacy and Security Model

- Sandboxed app, local browser engine — task data not stored on Moonshot servers
- Signed installers with published SHA-256 checksums
- Optional BYO API key stored locally
- Open source, auditable on GitHub

## Target Audience

- Developers wanting parallel whole-repo coding and agentic execution
- Researchers needing large-scale parallel data gathering
- Marketers analyzing many competitors at once
- Investors pulling financial data at scale
- Claude Code / Cursor / OpenClaw users wanting a 5×-cheaper agentic backend
- Teams wanting swarm orchestration without CLI complexity

## Comparable Tools

- **Kimi Code CLI (official)** — Moonshot's official CLI for K2.7, terminal-based, single-agent default
- **Kilo Code** — VS Code extension supporting K2.7 among 500+ models
- **OpenClaw** — open-source autonomous agent, supports K2.7 as backend
- **Cursor / Windsurf** — IDE coding assistants, single-agent
- **Claude Code (Opus 4.8)** — Anthropic agentic CLI, higher cost, single-agent

This app's positioning combines 300-agent parallel swarm, native desktop UX, MCP Hive multiplying K2.7's best-in-class tool use, Swarm Bridge into existing tools, and free proxy-pool access — a combination not offered by any existing Kimi tool.

## Common Questions

**Is it free?** Yes, Swarm mode runs through a built-in proxy pool; most users never pay. BYO Moonshot key for unlimited.

**Why does K2.7 beat Opus 4.8?** 81.1% vs 76.4% on MCPMark Verified (tool use), at ~5× lower cost per token.

**Can my PC handle 300 agents?** Yes — cloud cluster does the work, desktop orchestrates. 8GB RAM is plenty.

**Is it safe?** Sandboxed, signed installers, SHA-256 checksums, local browser engine.

**Swarm Bridge?** K2.7's Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible API lets the swarm back Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenClaw at 5× lower cost.

**Mac support?** Yes, signed notarized universal binary, native Apple Silicon.
